sections.heading: tyPushModifier
sections.content: ThetyPushmodifier is an alternative to 3ds Max’s built-in Push modifier, that allows you to specify a push direction, rather than simply pushing vertices along their normals.

sections.heading: Push Rollout
sections.content:

Push elements: when selected, mesh elements will be pushed out from the center of the mesh.

Push vertices: when selected, mesh vertices will be pushed along the specified direction.

Push splines: when selected, spline knots will be pushed in the specified manner.

Use vertex selection: when enabled, only selected vertices will be affected.

sections.heading: Push vertices
sections.content:
Vertex normals: vertices will be pushed along the direction of their normals.Local space vector: vertices will be pushed along the specified vector in local space.World space vector: vertices will be pushed along the specified vector in world space.Open edges outwards: vertices on open edges will be pushed outwards, perpendicular to the normals of their adjacent faces.Outward from meshes: vertices will be pushed away from the closest point on the specified meshes.

Vertex normals: vertices will be pushed along the direction of their normals.

Local space vector: vertices will be pushed along the specified vector in local space.

World space vector: vertices will be pushed along the specified vector in world space.

Open edges outwards: vertices on open edges will be pushed outwards, perpendicular to the normals of their adjacent faces.

Outward from meshes: vertices will be pushed away from the closest point on the specified meshes.

Amount: the amount to push vertices along the specified direction.X/Y/Z: the user-defined push vector.

Amount: the amount to push vertices along the specified direction.

X/Y/Z: the user-defined push vector.

sections.heading: Push elements
sections.content:
Outwards from center: elements will be pushed away from the center of the mesh, relative to their distance to the center.Outwards from gizmo: elements will be pushed away from the center of the sub-object gizmo, relative to their distance to the center.Outward above gizmo: elements will be pushed along the z-axis of the sub-object gizmo, if their center is above the gizmo, relative to their distance from the gizmo along the z-axis.Using element bbox: the center of each element will be the center of each element’s bounding box.Using element verts: the center of each element will be the average position of its vertices.Amount %: controls how far each mesh element should be pushed out (this value is a multiplier on the relative distance - calculated by the given element push mode specified above).Variation %: the per-particle percentage of variation to apply.Distance: elements within this distance from the specified center will be fully affected.Falloff: the effect on elements beyond the base distance, but within this falloff distance, will diminish according to the inverse-square law.Allow non-manifold edges: when enabled, non-manifold edges (edges with 3+ adjacent faces) will be used in the element flood-fill algorithm.

Outwards from center: elements will be pushed away from the center of the mesh, relative to their distance to the center.

Outwards from gizmo: elements will be pushed away from the center of the sub-object gizmo, relative to their distance to the center.

Outward above gizmo: elements will be pushed along the z-axis of the sub-object gizmo, if their center is above the gizmo, relative to their distance from the gizmo along the z-axis.

Using element bbox: the center of each element will be the center of each element’s bounding box.

Using element verts: the center of each element will be the average position of its vertices.

Amount %: controls how far each mesh element should be pushed out (this value is a multiplier on the relative distance - calculated by the given element push mode specified above).

Distance: elements within this distance from the specified center will be fully affected.

Falloff: the effect on elements beyond the base distance, but within this falloff distance, will diminish according to the inverse-square law.

Allow non-manifold edges: when enabled, non-manifold edges (edges with 3+ adjacent faces) will be used in the element flood-fill algorithm.

The edges in a manifold (non-degenerate) mesh will only ever have up to 2 adjacent faces (open edges have 1 adjacent face, closed edges have 2 adjacent faces). In a non-manifold (degenerate) mesh, some edges may have 3 or more adjacent faces. If the element flood-fill algorithm (the algorithm that is used to find connected mesh elements by following edge-face adjacencies) is not set to recognize non-manifold edges, this can lead to situations where faces connected by non-manifold edges may be treated as separate elements, even if they appear to be connected. Alternatively, if non-manifold edges are recognized by the algorithm, this can lead to situations where seemingly-separate elements connected only by a single edge will be considered part of the same element.

sections.heading: Uniqueness
sections.content: Seed: the seed value for all varied parameters.

sections.heading: Push splines
sections.content:
Clip: splines will be pushed using the Clipper offsetting method.

When “clip” mode is selected, spline knots will be projected along the Z-axis of the spline normal. This will flatten knots along the shortest axis of their OOBB.

Simple: splines will be pushed along their knot tangent vectors.Join mode: controls the extrapolated perimeter shape of splines.End mode: controls whether splines will be offset as closed lines/polygons or open lines with the (specified) end shape.Amount: the amount to push spline knots in the specified mode.

Simple: splines will be pushed along their knot tangent vectors.

Join mode: controls the extrapolated perimeter shape of splines.

End mode: controls whether splines will be offset as closed lines/polygons or open lines with the (specified) end shape.

Amount: the amount to push spline knots in the specified mode.
